Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week — ElmStreet’s product team liked the latency profile and the cost projections. Security asked me to start a short evaluation/MAP to capture required gates before we move to procurement. High level asks from them: SOC 2 evidence, SIG/CAIQ answers for the features we intend to use, a signed DPA w/ a 90-day default retention tier, and confirmation of private VPC routing for traffic between our prod systems and Redwood Dedicated.

Can you share a suggested MAP with milestone dates and the artifacts we should expect at each step? We’re trying to close procurement by early March, so a tight runway.

Best,
Alex

Alex —

Really appreciate the clear asks. I’ve attached a one-page MAP (redwood-elmstreet-map-v1.pdf) that breaks the run-to-close into four milestones: Discovery / POA, Security Evidence & DPA, Pilot / Canary, Contract Close. Quick notes specific to your list:

- SOC 2: we can provide our latest Type II report and an SOC 2 bridge letter.
- SIG/CAIQ: we’ll complete a scoped CAIQ focused on token handling, KV cache behavior, and VPC networking.
- DPA: we can circulate our standard DPA with the option for a customer redline; we typically agree retention tiers per customer (default 90 days).
- VPC: private VPC peering is supported for Dedicated deployments — we will include a network diagram and certificate-of-compliance notes.

Proposed milestone dates (aiming for your early-March procurement):
1) Discovery & MAP sign-off: by 2027-01-20
2) Evidence delivery (SOC2 + CAIQ) & DPA redline: by 2027-01-25
3) Pilot/canary testing (2 weeks): start 2027-02-01, complete 2027-02-14
4) Contract execution: target 2027-03-03

Marissa (security) and Priyom (solutions) are looped for evidence delivery and technical plan. If the dates look tight we can prioritize the DPA and SOC2 evidence first so procurement can start while pilot scheduling follows.

Next step: Marissa — can you confirm the specific evidentiary files we’ll push and whether we need any extra attestations for network isolation?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber

Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Alex / Jonas —

Adding more operational detail on the security/compliance gates so everyone has a concrete checklist. I’ll upload the artifacts to the MAP drive link once this thread confirms scope.

Required artifacts (deliverable + acceptable form):
- SOC 2 Type II (most recent period): PDF report + bridge letter (if report period does not cover go-live).
- SIG/CAIQ: completed spreadsheet (we will provide a scoped CAIQ focusing on endpoints used; see attached SIG-CAIQ-response-elmstreet.xlsx).
- DPA: Redwood standard DPA with customer redline tracked separately (we expect one round of redlines unless new clauses introduced).
- Data retention & deletion: documented retention tiers (90/30/7 days options) and the API/console controls for retention. Need customer confirmation on which tier they want as default for the pilot vs production.
- Network isolation evidence: VPC peering diagram, IPSec certs or peering ACL snapshot, and a planned IP allowlist for ElmStreet environments.
- Access controls: list of roles and SSO/OAuth integration guide; will provide a short CSV of admin accounts and RBAC matrix.

Acceptance criteria to transition between milestones:
- From Discovery -> Evidence: ElmStreet confirms scope + signs MAP one-pager.
- Evidence -> Pilot: ElmStreet acknowledges receipt of SOC2 PDF + CAIQ and provides DPA redline or acceptance. If DPA redline is returned, legal review window is 5 business days.
- Pilot -> Contract: Pilot metrics meet agreed-upon SLOs (tokens/sec, p95 latency) and no outstanding security blockers.

Timeline feasibility: we can deliver SOC2 PDF and the scoped CAIQ by 2027-01-20 if we prioritize this thread. DPA redline turnaround depends on your legal team; if you can return redlines by 2027-01-22 we can commit to the pilot start date on 2027-02-01.

Attachments referenced: SOC2-report-2024.pdf, SIG-CAIQ-response-elmstreet.xlsx

Marissa Cole
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Note: For retention, please specify whether ElmStreet requires any custom retention hold periods (e.g., regulatory holds) — that may extend DPA review time.

From: Samira Khan <security@elmstreet.com>

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our legal/security teams: 

1) DPA: we will do a single redline pass. Our preference is: 90-day default retention for pilot, 365-day for production. We’ll attach our redline by 2027-01-22.
2) CAIQ: can you confirm that the scoped CAIQ will explicitly call out KV cache retention and whether cache snapshots are stored? We need explicit language for ephemeral cache TTLs.
3) SOC2: we prefer a signed PDF with the auditor contact info.
4) VPC: we need the peering diagram and the proposed IP ranges by 2027-01-20 so our networking team can provision routes.

We’ll aim to return the DPA redline and a short project plan from our side by 2027-01-22. If Redwood can provide the CAIQ items and the network plan earlier (2027-01-18) that will help unblock our procurement queue.

Regards,
Samira Khan
Senior Security Engineer
ElmStreet Systems
